topic: Probe-ID: complete identification from known disturbing mechanism probes in finite ADMGs. Each accessible branch applies known separable local input/output kernels, with marginal informational completeness but not necessarily passive observation or perfect intervention. For a causal query, construct a terminating district calculus returning a dual-frame-invariant arithmetic functional of accessible tensors or strictly positive same-observed-alphabet probe-hedge twins with an explicit latent bound; prove soundness, completeness, ordinary-ID reduction, complexity, and regular inference. Use the binary front-door ADMG X->M->Y with X<->Y, mediator probe columns (3/4,1/4),(1/4,3/4), tensor q=(33,15,7,9,9,7,15,33)/128, responses (3/16,11/16),(5/16,13/16), and targets 3/8,5/8. Ananke is the software consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A split-port tensor reduction expresses accessible laws and do-queries as contractions of one causally constrained kernel. For the finite bow X->Y,X<->Y with arbitrary separable X probes and MIC terminal observation, the query is identified exactly when its response coefficient lies in the probe-matrix row span; failure yields strictly positive twins using |X| latent states. Every one of 1,764 tested minimal binary MIC menus fails both bow targets. Separate legal examples give identical accessible laws with different targets and show naive signed inversion can leave the probability simplex, while the front-door arithmetic checks exactly. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a district local-to-global theorem whose legal contractions and nullspace obstructions preserve independent latent sources and extend to bounded positive mechanisms. EARLY KILL TEST: Require the first reachability rule to reproduce the exact bow row-span oracle, its positive twins, full-matrix tomography success, then survive a three-node confounded chain and adjacent districts. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_disturbprobe_admg_complete_id.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does marginal informational completeness of known separable local probes admit a sound-and-complete terminating district calculus for every finite ADMG and atomic causal query, while reproducing the exact bow row-span oracle?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves identification from marginally informationally complete instruments for Markovian models and leaves the corresponding ADMG theory open.
source_refs.author: Isaac Friend, Aleks Kissinger, Robert W. Spekkens, Elie Wolfe

source_refs.claim: Reachability, fixing, intrinsic sets, and district kernels characterize ordinary ADMG identification from a passive observed law.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: The delivered local recursion is proved sound but not complete

open_problems.why_unsolved: Friend et al. recover Markovian mechanisms by nodewise topological induction, whereas ordinary ADMG fixing extracts intrinsic district kernels from a passive law. Probe data are instead known contractions of a causally constrained split-port tensor, and dual-frame inversions can produce signed arrays that are not stochastic kernels. The prior district-closed run independently found that locally projected district faces can outer-relax the true multi-district compatibility fiber. The missing proof is a gluing theorem showing that every legal local reconstruction preserves shared-observable compatibility and independence of district exogenous sources, with a complete obstruction when it does not.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A typed terminating recursion returning either a dual-frame-invariant arithmetic functional of accessible tensors or a terminal target-varying certificate, with soundness, completeness, ordinary-ID reduction, bow-oracle agreement, and an explicit graph-and-alphabet complexity bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation begins with imperfect or disturbing collection and formulates accessibility through local instruments, exactly the narrative the ADMG extension needs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Passive observation is only one local instrument -> marginally informationally complete probes recover Markovian mechanisms -> latent districts break nodewise induction -> a complete probe-ID calculus for ADMG queries is needed

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt fixing, reachability recursion, intrinsic-district factorization, and fixing-order invariance, replacing kernels extracted from p(V) by kernels reconstructed from probe contractions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its district recursion is the local-to-global skeleton needed for the requested identifying functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over recursive c-component decomposition and hedge-based completeness, replacing observational equality by equality of all accessible probe tensors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The new calculus must reduce to ordinary ID and needs a probe analogue of its decisive failure certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt generalized sequential back-door representations and multiply robust remainder analysis to functionals assembled from independently sampled probe regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies limit theory for causal functionals assembled from multiple observational and interventional input laws.

open_problems.open_problem: Can every target-varying null direction exposed by a terminal probe-calculus failure be realized by two strictly positive finite SCMs on the same observed alphabets, with mutually independent district latent sources and an explicit latent-cardinality bound?

source_refs.claim: For generalized identification, positivity is necessary for soundness and invalidates the earlier completeness proof, requiring a new complete algorithm.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Ordinary nonidentifiability is characterized by hedges and proved using observationally indistinguishable models with different intervention responses.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.excerpt: explicit paired-SCM extraction requires a new sample-point, representation, decoding, and correctness architecture
Districtwise atom probabilities cannot simply be selected independently

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary hedge twins need agree only on p(V), while probe indistinguishability imposes many additional multilinear equalities. A local tensor-nullspace perturbation can leave the probability simplex, couple exogenous sources that the ADMG requires to be independent, or lose its target contrast after smoothing. Prior SCM runs encountered the same failed lift from local fiber directions or projected hedge pairs to legal global models. Positivity is therefore structural here: the proof must jointly construct latent variables and mechanisms, preserve every probe contraction exactly, and remain in a bounded positive interior.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive probe-hedge theorem converting every legal terminal null certificate into same-alphabet strictly positive twins with independent district sources, identical accessible tensors, unequal target values, and a graph-and-alphabet-dependent latent-support bound, or a minimal counterexample disproving such conversion.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats positivity as a theorem-level fault line in identification completeness rather than a routine regularity condition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A complete identification claim is proposed -> missing positivity makes its rules unsound -> imposing positivity breaks the old completeness witness -> probe-ID needs positive source-separable nonidentifiability twins

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the parity-based hedge construction so equality holds for every legal probe contraction rather than only the passive margin.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the canonical completeness-by-twins strategy and the graph obstruction the new theorem must refine.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite response-function canonicalization and polynomial equality constraints to search for an interior feasible perturbation and control latent support.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Probe equality and target separation are polynomial constraints over finite causal response types, matching the required twin object.

open_problems.open_problem: Is causal-query identifiability from observed-node probes invariant across latent-DAG, canonical independent-bidirected-source, and equation-system interpretations of the same finite ADMG?

source_refs.claim: The probe paper sketches ADMG causal structures as margins of DAG-based process models but leaves a thorough ADMG treatment to future work.
source_refs.author: Isaac Friend, Aleks Kissinger, Robert W. Spekkens, Elie Wolfe

source_refs.claim: The equation-system model and common latent-DAG interpretations of an ADMG differ in general, though equivalences hold in special subclasses.
source_refs.author: Qingyuan Zhao

source_refs.claim: Ordinary causal-effect identification is expressed through latent-projection ADMG intrinsic kernels without choosing a particular hidden-variable expansion.
source_refs.author: Thomas S. Richardson, Robin J. Evans, James M. Robins, Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ordinary ID can be formulated on the latent-projection ADMG, but disturbing probes touch the input and output ports of observed mechanisms and may reveal distinctions suppressed by that projection. Friend et al. do not fix a complete ADMG semantics, while Zhao shows that common ADMG model interpretations diverge outside special subclasses. A proposed calculus can therefore be sound relative to one latent ontology yet fail for another unless the probe response maps themselves are preserved by the representation change.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equivalence theorem preserving accessible-tensor equality and causal-query equality under explicit transformations among the three ADMG semantics, with necessary conditions, or a smallest finite graph and probe menu separating their identification frontiers.

writing_exemplar.why: It foregrounds the substantive modeling choice hidden by a single ADMG notation and organizes the competing semantics explicitly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ADMGs summarize latent confounding -> several non-equivalent causal semantics hide under the notation -> ordinary results sometimes avoid choosing among them -> probe-ID must prove semantic invariance or exhibit separation

method_exemplars.technique: Extend unconfounded-expansion and model-union equivalence arguments by transporting each observed-node probe response map along the expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is precisely an equivalence or separation between ADMG model classes after enriching their observable interface.

method_exemplars.technique: Use fixing-sequence invariance and intrinsic-kernel characterization as the benchmark property that a probe-enriched semantic translation must preserve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the representation-independent ordinary-ID frontier against which probe semantics should be compared.

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite ADMG and a fixed legal probe menu that does not point-identify a causal query, what is the sharp identified interval over bounded strictly positive SCMs reproducing the full accessible probe tensor?

source_refs.claim: Finite discrete causal questions with incomplete or mismeasured data reduce to polynomial programs that return sharp bounds and point identification when the interval collapses.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Partial counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental distributions can be converted to an equivalent polynomial program.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.excerpt: Develop the deferred sharp off-span identified-set program, including endpoint-attaining compatible SCMs
ordinary row span alone can miss identification when the menu forces response profiles to zero

open_problems.why_unsolved: AutoBounds-style methods encode ordinary observed, experimental, missing, or mismeasured distributions, but a local probe branch contracts both incoming and outgoing mechanism alphabets. The evidence-map proof must therefore preserve shared mechanisms and independent district sources rather than replace them by one unrestricted response type. An off-span separator proves only non-singleton identification: sharp endpoints must optimize over the exact SCM-realizable fiber, where positivity bounds, forced-zero faces, and cross-district polynomial compatibility exclude many unconstrained tensor-nullspace directions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite response-type parameterization and equivalent polynomial or polyhedral-on-strata optimization whose extrema are the sharp query endpoints, with endpoint-attaining positive SCMs or dual sharpness certificates and collapse exactly on the probe-identifiable fiber.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames automated sharp bounds as the principled output when nonstandard finite causal evidence defeats analytic identification formulas.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real causal evidence departs from textbook observation -> analytic identified sets become intractable -> response-function programs automate sharp bounds -> probe tensors require a legal district-aware evidence map

method_exemplars.technique: Port finite response-function canonicalization, polynomial evidence constraints, dual relaxation, and spatial branch-and-bound, replacing ordinary data constraints by probe contractions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The interval is a sharp polynomial image of a finite causal compatibility fiber constrained by observed tensor coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt arbitrary-data-source counterfactual factorization and its equivalence proof to a source map made of local input-output contractions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already handles heterogeneous causal inputs; the changed step is the probe evidence map rather than the optimization target.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt calibrated projection and bootstrap relaxation of sample moment constraints to confidence sets for probe-program bound endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: With sampled probe tensors, each endpoint is a projection of a constrained partially identified parameter vector.

open_problems.open_problem: For a probe-ID functional in a finite ADMG, what is the semiparametric efficiency bound and can regular inference remain dual-frame invariant across rank changes, district-calculus branch ties, and singular multinomial covariance?

source_refs.claim: Generalized-identification functionals can be represented through generalized sequential back-door adjustments and estimated with multiply robust asymptotic theory.
source_refs.author: Yonghan Jung, Iván Díaz, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Influence-function estimators, double robustness, and efficiency bounds are derived for broad classes of effects identified in hidden-variable DAGs.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: The studentized singularity-robust projection theorem remains open
Inference is asserted only where branch guards and algebraic operations are separated from singular boundaries

open_problems.why_unsolved: Probe reconstruction uses nonunique dual frames and can require ill-conditioned signed inversions before composing district functionals. Population dual-frame invariance does not imply invariance of an estimated influence function, and two equivalent frames may have diverging coefficients near rank loss. Existing ADMG and gID estimators begin from observed or perfect-intervention laws, not independently sampled probe tensors linked by known kernels. Prior proposals likewise obtain ordinary delta-method inference only away from branch boundaries, leaving changing-rank nuisance fibers, tied reachability decisions, and singular covariance untreated.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of the probe-observed tangent space and efficient influence function, plus a representation-invariant one-step, targeted, or inverted-test confidence procedure with uniform coverage across regular, weak-rank, branch-tie, and singular-covariance sequences and a root-n efficiency result on regular strata.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the practical gap between complete multi-source identification and usable finite-sample estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Data fusion identifies effects in principle -> raw identifying expressions are difficult to estimate -> a common representation yields robust limit theory -> probe-ID needs frame-invariant inference under known disturbing kernels

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt hidden-variable tangent-space projections, primal-fixing influence functions, and weight-based estimators to probe-reconstructed intrinsic kernels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies efficiency theory for ADMG-identified effects, including front-door-type functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singularity-robust moment standardization and drifting-sequence size proofs to profiled probe-balancing coefficients.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Probe tensors have structural covariance degeneracies and weak directions that invalidate ordinary studentization.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate directional derivatives of the piecewise-smooth returned functional and bootstrap through active-branch ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A terminating calculus is nonsmooth precisely where reachability or active-face branches tie.

open_problems.open_problem: Given a finite ADMG, a causal query, and a priced catalogue of known separable probe kernels, what minimum-cost probe menu is sufficient for identification without enumerating all menus?

source_refs.claim: Minimum-cost perfect-intervention design for a specific causal effect is NP-complete and admits a hitting-set formulation with logarithmic approximation.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Proxy experiment design chooses lower-cost perfect-intervention targets whose distributions identify an effect, using graph-based reformulations and pruning.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

source_refs.excerpt: No located result characterizes minimum-cost acquisition of dependent realizable Layer-3 regime blocks
state an explicit finite enumeration/complexity bound for the feasible-basis computation

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing design results select variables for perfect interventions and reduce graphical obstruction coverage to hitting set. Probe catalogues add an algebraic dimension: menus touching the same vertices can have different row spans, conditioning, active faces, and ability to distinguish district kernels, while one probe changes a dependent family of tensor contractions rather than adding an independent row. The first proof step that changes is the coverage oracle, which must measure query-specific information after legal district reductions and preserve causal compatibility.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient probe-menu criterion with a polynomially checkable identifying certificate and dual insufficiency certificate, an exact complexity classification, and an exact or approximation algorithm whose bow specialization is the response-vector row-span oracle.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly turns failed passive identification into a resource-allocation problem and separates identifiability from minimum-cost design.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observation may not identify an effect -> experiments can restore identification but are costly -> choose the cheapest sufficient intervention collection -> extend the design object from perfect targets to legal probe kernels

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt obstruction coverage and weighted hitting-set reduction after replacing the hedge-hit oracle by a complete probe-ID reachability oracle.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems minimize experimental resources subject to exact identification of one causal query.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt district-wise pruning and proxy-selection reformulations while augmenting each candidate with the query-relevant rank contribution of its known kernel.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest design literature for indirect experiments chosen to identify a target effect.

method_exemplars.technique: Attach multi-source influence-function variance and sample-allocation costs to menus that are equivalent at the population-identification level.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The practical design frontier should distinguish algebraically sufficient menus by the inferential quality of their regime estimators.

literature_map:
Friend, Kissinger, Spekkens, and Wolfe (Entropy 2025, DOI 10.3390/e27070732) is the exact anchor: local noisy or disturbing instruments, process-theoretic contractions, and marginal informational completeness.
Its main theorem recovers Markovian DAG mechanisms; it explicitly leaves a thorough ADMG treatment and the broader identification theory open.
Friend and Kissinger (Physical Review A 2024, arXiv:2311.08882) supplies earlier process-tomographic causal-identification machinery under restricted instruments.
Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006; JMLR 2008) provide ordinary ID and counterfactual completeness with hedge-based nonidentifiability.
Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (Annals of Statistics 2023, arXiv:1701.06686) provide fixing, reachability, intrinsic sets, and nested district kernels for ADMG margins.
Bareinboim and Pearl (UAI 2012, arXiv:1210.4842) establish complete z-identification from surrogate perfect experiments.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) extend identification to arbitrary collections of observational and perfect-interventional distributions through gID.
Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (UAI 2022, arXiv:2206.01081) show positivity changes gID soundness and breaks the earlier completeness proof before repairing it.
Correa and Bareinboim (AAAI 2020, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v34i06.6567) give sigma-calculus for stochastic policies, but not inversion from disturbing probe tensors.
Zhao (arXiv:2501.03048) shows common causal interpretations of an ADMG differ in general, creating a semantic-invariance obligation for probe-ID.
Duarte et al. (JASA 2024, arXiv:2109.13471) reduce finite discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs with response-type canonicalization.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022) extend polynomial partial identification to arbitrary observational and experimental sources, not local input-output contractions.
Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (JMLR 2025, arXiv:2205.02232) and Elahi et al. (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.05330) study minimum-cost perfect or proxy intervention targets, not kernel menus.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022, arXiv:2003.12659) give ADMG influence-function theory; Jung et al. (NeurIPS 2023) give multiply robust gID estimation.
No located paper closes finite latent-confounded probe-ID with a complete district calculus, bounded positive probe-hedges, sharp probe bounds, semantic invariance, kernel-menu design, or dual-frame-invariant inference.
